column1: # OUTSIDE_SPITBOL_BASELINE.tsv -- spitbol_testpgms: programs the ONE ORACLE itself does not run, so they are
# OUTSIDE the graded baseline and OUT OF THE DENOMINATOR. Lon 2026-09-08: the leaderboard divides by the
# programs SPITBOL runs clean, and a program SPITBOL cannot run is recorded per program with SPITBOL's own
# error AND a source check. Written coo 2026-09-08; test_snoflake_suite.sh is the shape.
# MEASURED, not declared: test_snobol4_spitbol_testpgms_suite.sh runs sbl -bf on every program each run and
# cross-checks this file against what it saw, printing STALE (recorded here but sbl answered it cleanly) or
# UNRECORDED (sbl refuses it and this file is silent). UNGRADABLE.tsv mirrors this file row for row and the
# runner says so aloud when the two drift.
# THE SOURCE CHECK IS THE POINT, not decoration: each row quotes the exact statement at the line SPITBOL
# names and says why SPITBOL declines it. Every one of these six is legal SNOBOL4 that SPITBOL refuses on
# environment or on a name collision -- not a program that is wrong. That is what makes it a baseline
# question rather than a defect.
# Oracle: /home/resources/x64/bin/sbl -bf, run 2026-09-08 in a scratch copy with the suite's own testpgms.in.
# Columns: name <TAB> ORACLE_REFUSES <TAB> does not run in SPITBOL: <error, file(line)>; source checked <date> (<who>): stmt <line> <source> -- <why>
test2.spt
column3: does not run in SPITBOL: ERROR 214 -- bad label or misplaced continuation line, test2.spt(238); source checked 2026-09-08 (coo): stmt 238 `.                                                          ERROR()` -- a lone period in the label column as a continuation marker; SPITBOL reads column 1 as a label and rejects the line before the program runs. ⛔ NONDETERMINISTIC, and this row corrected itself the same hour: a direct sbl -bf run at 2026-09-08 gave ERROR 214 at line 238, so the first draft of this row claimed the refusal was deterministic -- the very next runner pass got rc=231 with no listing instead. One observation is not a determinism claim. Both paths refuse the program and both put it outside the baseline, which is why the classification is stable even though the symptom is not. ⛔⭐ REASON FALSIFIED AND REPLACED 2026-09-14 (cfo), MEASURED IN THREE ARMS RATHER THAN READ: A LONE PERIOD IN COLUMN 1 IS NOT WHAT SPITBOL REJECTS -- it accepts lone-period continuations everywhere, including thirteen of them inside test5.spt, which compiles and runs clean. Three-arm probe against sbl -bf, one statement each: (a) an INCOMPLETE statement continued by a lone period is ACCEPTED and prints its answer; (b) a COMPLETE statement followed by a lone-period continuation raises ERROR 212, a different error; (c) a statement TERMINATED BY THE SEPARATOR ';' and then continued by a lone period raises ERROR 214 -- this row's error, reproduced in three lines. THE TRIGGER IS THE SEMICOLON, NOT THE PERIOD: test2.spt line 237 ends with ';' and line 238 continues it. The earlier reason quoted the right error at the right line and described the wrong cause, and it stood from 2026-09-08; see .github/FINDING-2026-09-14-cfo-a-number-is-not-evidence-for-the-sentence-it-appears-in.md. The classification is unchanged -- ERROR 214 is a COMPILE refusal, so all 260 lines are refused and the program stays OUTSIDE the baseline -- and the decomposition of test2 is NOT yet done.

column1: test4.spt
column3: does not run in SPITBOL: ERROR 116 -- inappropriate file specification for input, test4.spt(65); source checked 2026-09-08 (coo): stmt 65 `INPUT(.INPUT,,72)` -- a three-argument INPUT association with an EMPTY file specification and a record length; legal SNOBOL4, but SPITBOL requires a real file argument, so it refuses the association rather than the program's logic. ⛔⭐ RE-MEASURED 2026-09-14 (cfo, CEO-725): THE ROW'S ERROR NUMBER AND LINE ARE RIGHT AND ITS DESCRIPTION IS WRONG IN KIND -- sbl -bf exits rc=0 on this program. It RUNS, aborts at statement 37 of 99, and prints its own fatal-termination accounting, which is the ORACLE_ACCOUNTING_IN_OUTPUT class (CEO-724), not a refusal. WITH THAT ONE ASSOCIATION REMOVED THE ORACLE RUNS THE WHOLE PROGRAM AND PRINTS 1366 LINES. The program is now decomposed into the master as tpgm4_syntactic_recognizer, DEFERRED in corpus/tests/snobol4/PENDING.md to row snobol4-fence-then-an-operand-then-an-alternation-in-a-pattern-variable-never-backtracks because SCRIP disagrees with the oracle on exactly FOUR of those 1366 lines: it says SYNTACTIC ERROR where SPITBOL says NO SYNTACTIC ERROR, for every statement carrying a two-part goto. This row stays OUTSIDE the TPgm baseline -- the whole program still aborts under sbl -- and what changed is that its content is graded somewhere instead of nowhere.

column1: test6.spt
column3: does not run in SPITBOL: ERROR 248 -- attempted redefinition of system function, test6.spt(16); source checked 2026-09-08 (coo), REASON CORRECTED 2026-09-13 (ceo CEO-725) after probing the oracle directly rather than reading the line: stmt 16 `DATA('ITEM(COUNT,TOP)')` -- the collision is THE DATA TYPE NAME `ITEM`, which is itself a SPITBOL builtin, and NOT the generated accessors. Measured on sbl -bf: DATA('FOO(COUNT,TOP)') is ACCEPTED, so COUNT and TOP collide with nothing; DATA('ITEM(CNT,TP)') with no colliding field names at all still raises 248. The earlier reason named the wrong half of the statement and stood for five days. ⛔ NOT AN ORACLE REFUSAL EITHER: sbl -bf exits rc=0 on this program -- it runs, dies at statement 4, and prints its own fatal-termination accounting, which is the ORACLE_ACCOUNTING_IN_OUTPUT class (CEO-724). Lon has since ruled all eight programs IN (CEO-725) and named the mechanism: decompose them into the master's one-liner and banner-block entries so each construct is graded on its own. ⛔⭐ RE-MEASURED 2026-09-14 (cfo): AND THE EARLIER NOTE'S OWN COUNT WAS RIGHT WHILE ITS DESCRIPTION WAS NOT -- the 40 lines this program prints after the abort are an &DUMP=2 dump of natural variables and keyword values, NOT program output. Removing the colliding DATA prototype exposes a SECOND blocker at line 20, the same INPUT association as test4/5/7, and past that the program still stops on ERROR 066 because it reads its own control data from a shared input file it no longer gets fixed-length records from. NOT YET DECOMPOSED for that reason; it is the only one of the five whose body does not become gradable by removing environment statements alone.

column1: test7.spt
column3: does not run in SPITBOL: ERROR 248 -- attempted redefinition of system function, test7.spt(10); source checked 2026-09-08 (coo): stmt 10 `DATA('SYMB(CHAR,LINK,ALT,ASSOC,SUCC)')` -- same class as test6: the prototype's CHAR accessor collides with SPITBOL's own CHAR, so the DATA statement is refused before execution. ⛔⭐ RE-MEASURED 2026-09-14 (cfo, CEO-725): sbl -bf exits rc=0. It RUNS, aborts at statement 1 of 142, and prints fatal-termination accounting -- ORACLE_ACCOUNTING_IN_OUTPUT (CEO-724), not a refusal. TWO statements block it, this one and the line-11 INPUT association; with both removed the oracle runs the SYMBOL TABLE GENERATOR whole, 1251 lines, and SCRIP IS BYTE-IDENTICAL TO IT IN BOTH MODES. The field rename CHAR -> CHR is the whole cure and a field spelling is arbitrary where the collision is not. Absorbed as tpgm7_symbol_table_generator (corpus 7443a1aa8). Stays OUTSIDE the TPgm baseline; its content is now graded.
